_how_to_use: PASTE ONLY THE `prompt` FIELD INTO THE IMAGE MODEL. Nothing else in this file is for the model. Pasting the whole file produced a collage of several captioned slides, because `renditions_wanted` lists two sizes, `framing.aspect_ratios` lists two ratios, and headline_in_app / caption_in_app are text - the model read all of that as a brief to draw multiple frames with words on them. Those fields are for the render pipeline and for whoever writes the app copy.
_source_image_note: Save the image you keep in this folder named `02_welcome_2_know_where_you_stand` with whatever extension the model gave you - .jpg, .png, .jpeg and .webp are all accepted. Only the NAME has to match this file; the extension does not. lessons/scripts/tutor_images.py then renders it to renders/02_welcome_2_know_where_you_stand/ as slide_1080x1920 (9:16 phone slide) and card_1080x1350 (4:5). Renditions are always written as PNG regardless of the source format.
audience: a parent or guardian setting up for a learner
caption_in_app: A quick check before and after each class shows what you already know - no pressure, just progress.
intent: a parent finally able to see how it is going
prompt: A single photograph, one continuous scene, filling the whole frame. A Coloured South African mother in her forties in a plain blouse and cardigan, sitting alone on a couch in the evening, phone in one hand held at a natural angle so the screen is not readable, with a calm attentive expression - the look of someone reading a short update and understanding it. A mug on the side table. Soft lamplight, quiet room, no clutter. photorealistic documentary photograph, natural available light, real skin texture, candid and unposed, shot on a full-frame camera, 35mm, f/2.8, true-to-life colour.
negative_prompt: any text, letters, numbers, words, signage, logos, watermarks, user-interface elements, phone screens showing apps, charts or graphs, cartoon, illustration, 3d render, cgi, airbrushed skin, plastic sheen, cinematic colour grade, film still look, motion blur, lens flare, extra fingers, malformed hands, distorted faces, stock-photo smiles, American classrooms, generic 'African' styling, collage, multiple panels, split screen, side-by-side frames, contact sheet, grid of images, storyboard, several phone mockups, device frames, app screenshots, before-and-after, picture-in-picture, borders, margins, framed print, shirtless, bare chest, bare back, no shirt, undressed, pyjamas

_pipeline_only._note: NOT model input - read by the render script and the app.

framing.composition: subject in the lower two thirds, calm uncluttered space in the upper third where the slide's headline and caption sit - the image must never compete with the copy
framing.safe_area: keep the top 28% and bottom 18% visually quiet: the headline sits above, the button below

_casting_note: Cast deliberately (owner, 2026-07-30). The prompts said only 'a South African teenager'/'parent', so the model defaulted and every slide came back Black and male. The onboarding carousel is the first thing anyone sees on a national platform - a learner should be able to find themselves in it. students/01 and students/04 keep their approved casting; majority representation is right, it just cannot be the only representation.
